girard-triangle.title: Deceit, Desire, and the Novel
girard-triangle.author: René Girard
girard-triangle.reference: 1961; Yvonne Freccero translation, 1965. Chapter I, “Triangular Desire”: mediator, object, and subject.

girard-models.title: Deceit, Desire, and the Novel
girard-models.author: René Girard
girard-models.reference: Chapter I, “Triangular Desire”: external and internal mediation; the mediator as obstacle.

girard-being.title: Deceit, Desire, and the Novel
girard-being.author: René Girard
girard-being.reference: Chapter II, “Men Become Gods”: metaphysical desire and the imagined being of the mediator.

girard-distance.title: Deceit, Desire, and the Novel
girard-distance.author: René Girard
girard-distance.reference: Chapters III–IV, “The Metamorphoses of Desire” and “Master and Slave”: prestige, indifference, and reciprocal mediation.

girard-conversion.title: Deceit, Desire, and the Novel
girard-conversion.author: René Girard
girard-conversion.reference: Chapter XII, “Conclusion”: novelistic conversion and recognition of mediated desire. Literary interpretation, not a clinical treatment.

girard-double.title: Violence and the Sacred
girard-double.author: René Girard
girard-double.reference: 1972; Patrick Gregory translation, 1977. Chapter VI, “From Mimetic Desire to the Monstrous Double”: rivalry, reciprocity, and loss of differences.

girard-crisis.title: Violence and the Sacred
girard-crisis.author: René Girard
girard-crisis.reference: Chapters II–III, “The Sacrificial Crisis” and “Oedipus and the Surrogate Victim”: generalized conflict and collective convergence. A disputed anthropological reconstruction.

girard-ritual.title: Violence and the Sacred
girard-ritual.author: René Girard
girard-ritual.reference: Chapters IV and XI, “The Origins of Myth and Ritual” and “The Unity of All Rites”: ritual repetition and substitution. A contested hypothesis about cultural origins.

girard-persecution.title: The Scapegoat
girard-persecution.author: René Girard
girard-persecution.reference: 1982; Yvonne Freccero translation, 1986. Chapters I–II, “Guillaume de Machaut and the Jews” and “Stereotypes of Persecution”: crisis, accusation, and vulnerable victims.

girard-myth.title: The Scapegoat
girard-myth.author: René Girard
girard-myth.reference: Chapters III–IV, “What Is a Myth?” and “Violence and Magic”: persecution narratives and the attribution of disorder to victims.

girard-scape.title: I See Satan Fall Like Lightning
girard-scape.author: René Girard
girard-scape.reference: 2001 English edition, translated by James G. Williams. Chapter XII, “Scapegoat,” pp. 154–160; primary excerpt on misrecognition and scapegoating the scapegoaters.

girard-scholar.title: René Girard and Mimetic Theory
girard-scholar.author: Paul Gifford; St Andrews Encyclopaedia of Theology
girard-scholar.reference: 2023. Sections 1.2, 2.1–2.3, and 3.1–3.3: model relations, cooperative imitation, and scholarly disputes over universal origins claims.
